title: Racial Demographics in Florida
text:
Sarasota County is often perceived as demographically uniform: countywide, the median census tract is 84.4% non-Hispanic White. However, mapping race by census tract reveals sharp historical and geographic divides.









In North Sarasota, Census Tract 3—encompassing the historic African American community of Newtown—is 74.5% Black, surrounded by tracts that quickly drop into single digits. Newtown was established in the early 1900s during the Jim Crow era when Black residents were restricted to specific sections of the city, leaving a lasting demographic footprint that remains visible in 2020 Census data.

title: Racial Demographics in Florida
section: The Florida Panhandle: Plantation Legacy and Gadsden County
text:
The Florida Panhandle: Plantation Legacy and Gadsden County
Moving north, the Florida Panhandle illustrates how agricultural history shaped modern demographics. While coastal counties like Walton (4.4%) and Santa Rosa (5.7%) have small Black populations, Gadsden County (just west of Tallahassee) is 53.2% Black—making it Florida’s only majority-Black county.









As part of the antebellum “Black Belt,” Gadsden County was historically dedicated to plantation agriculture (notably shade tobacco and cotton). Today, that legacy is reflected in its distinctive majority-Black population compared to the rest of the Florida Panhandle.
